name: trivial_majority
notes: Trivial classifier: always predicts the majority class of the training set (PNEUMONIA). The majority class is a model parameter and is therefore estimated on train only, never on the set being evaluated. Under balanced accuracy it scores exactly 0.5 on any split by construction, so it is a floor rather than a meaningful target.

name: logreg_metadata
notes: Logistic regression on acquisition metadata only - width, height and aspect ratio - with no class weighting. Standardisation is fitted inside a Pipeline on the training split alone, so no statistics leak from validation or test. Without class weights the model minimises overall error and drifts towards the 72.7% majority class: it misclassifies 62 of the 268 validation NORMAL images, which is exactly what balanced accuracy penalises. Kept in the log as the control condition for run 003.

name: logreg_metadata_balanced
notes: Same model with class_weight=balanced, which weights each sample inversely to its class frequency and therefore aligns the training objective with the evaluation metric. Hypothesis confirmed: validation balanced accuracy rises from 0.7905 to 0.8602 against run 002. This is the reference figure of the project - roughly 0.86 of the task is solvable from acquisition metadata alone, without opening a single image, which measures how far the dataset is contaminated by provenance rather than driven by anatomy. Note also that a CNN never sees these numbers: after resizing they survive only indirectly, as resampling sharpness and geometric distortion, so this figure bounds the contamination of the dataset, not the behaviour of any given model.

name: cnn_baseline_gap
notes: Baseline CNN trained from scratch with a hand-written loop. Reported epoch is 28, the best validation balanced accuracy; the run was deliberately carried to 30 epochs with no early stopping so that the full shape of the curves would be visible. No overfitting: training and validation loss fall together and end within 0.006 of each other (0.092 against 0.098), and both were still descending when training stopped. The standard heuristic:small dataset, no regularisation, thirty epochs - predicted memorisation and was wrong.

name: cnn_flatten_head
notes: Same pipeline and same seed as run 004, one change: the global average pooling head replaced by flatten plus dense. Run as a diagnostic, not as a candidate model. Textbook overfitting: training loss reaches exactly 0.0000 by epoch 22, e training set is memorised, ile validation loss bottoms at 0.0715 on epoch 8 and then rises monotonically to 0.1748. The comparison with run 004 suggests that Global Average Pooling contributes to reducing overfitting. The instructive part is that balanced accuracy does NOT degrade while the loss diverges: it stays around 0.97 throughout.

name: cnn_gap_80_s42
notes: Run 004 extended to 80 epochs to test whether the absence of overfitting was real or premature. It was premature: validation loss bottoms at epoch 57 and rises afterwards, while training loss keeps falling, so the gap goes from none at epoch 30 (0.100 against 0.102) to sevenfold at epoch 80 (0.016 against 0.119). Global average pooling delays overfitting by roughly fifty epochs, it does not prevent it. Balanced accuracy again does not follow the loss. The apparent 1.3-point gain over run 004 is inflated: the best epoch out of 80 draws beats the best out of 30 even with no real improvement. Compared on ten-epoch block means the gain is about one point (0.953 against 0.964), for 2.7x the training time. From here on, runs of different length must be compared at a fixed epoch budget or on the mean of the last k epochs, never on their best epoch.

name: cnn_gap_40_s42
notes: First run under the fixed measurement protocol adopted for the next step: 40 epochs, and the reported score is the MEAN of the last five epochs rather than the best epoch, which is a biased estimator. 40 epochs sits past the useful zone and before the overfitting that run 006 located around epoch 57. This is the reference every next test configuration is compared against.

name: cnn_gap_40_s43
notes: Replication of run 007, identical in every respect except the torch seed. Its only purpose is to measure the noise floor. The two means differ by 0.17 points (0.9581 against 0.9564), an order of magnitude less than the 3-7 point swings seen between adjacent epochs: averaging the last five epochs absorbs most of that noise. Working rule for the rest: differences below roughly half a point are not treated as effects. Two runs give a rough estimate of spread, not a confidence interval, and the figure is reported as such. Combined reference: 0.957.

name: cnn_gap_40_cosine_s42
notes: Run 007 with a single change: CosineAnnealingLR over the full budget, T_max equal to the 40 epochs. Hypothesis: the 3-7 point swings between adjacent late epochs come from a learning rate that stays at 1e-3 until the end, so decaying it should stabilise the estimate. Late-epoch variability does drop, from std 0.0028 to 0.0019 over the last ten epochs, but this is guaranteed by construction rather than evidence for the hypothesis: with T_max equal to the budget the learning rate reaches zero and the weights stop moving, so the last epochs are near-copies of one another. The mean of the last five falls slightly, 0.9557 against 0.9581. Both final losses are higher than in run 007 (train 0.0710 against 0.0576, validation 0.0935 against 0.0903), which says the anneal stopped the optimisation while the model was still improving. Read together with run 010.

name: cnn_gap_40_cosine_s43
notes: Run 009 (seed replicate of 008), decisive for the choice. The schedule works as intended: late-epoch std collapses from 0.0220 (run 008) to 0.0032, curve flat and monotone — convergence, not just quiet. But the two annealed seeds sit 1.65 points apart (0.9557 vs 0.9392), against 0.17 points without the schedule: variance doesn't disappear within a run, it shifts between runs, by an order of magnitude. Cause visible at epoch 29: seed 43 at 0.924, seed 42 at 0.954; annealing freezes the model wherever it lands, and with LR at zero seed 43 can't escape the worse basin (in run 008 it kept moving, reaching 0.964). The difference between the two condition means (0.9573 vs 0.9475) is smaller than the spread between annealed seeds, so it's not a claimed effect.

name: cnn_gap_40_none_geom_photo_s42
notes: First augmentation run, at the 40-epoch budget used for the rest of Phase 4. Augmentations were chosen on anatomical grounds rather than by default: horizontal flip is excluded because the thorax is not symmetric. What is kept corresponds to real acquisition variability: small rotation, translation and scale for patient positioning and detector distance, mild brightness and contrast for exposure and dose. The result reads as a 1.06-point drop against run 007, but the run is not comparable: the best epoch is epoch 40, the last one available, and both losses are still descending. When the maximum falls on the edge of the budget the budget is the constraint, so this measures convergence speed, not quality. Superseded by run 014. Note also that train_loss ends above val_loss (0.1249 against 0.1120): expected rather than anomalous, since training images are distorted and validation images are not, so the two losses are no longer measured on the same distribution.

name: cnn_gap_40_none_geom_photo_s43
notes: Seed replication of run 011, same conclusion: best epoch is again epoch 40. The two augmented seeds sit 0.88 points apart against 0.17 for the unaugmented pair, so the apparent 1.42-point deficit of the condition is only marginally larger than its own spread. One qualitative difference is worth recording: validation loss spikes (0.315 and 0.390) coincide with drops in balanced accuracy (0.918, 0.893), the opposite of run 005 where loss diverged while the decision held. There the loss was calibration degrading; here loss and decision move together, so it is optimisation noise injected by the augmentation, not overfitting. Superseded by run 015.

name: cnn_gap_80_s43
notes: Seed replication of run 006 at the 80-epoch budget

name: cnn_gap_80_none_geom_photo_s42
notes: The augmentation experiment repeated at 80 epochs, after runs 011 and 012 showed the 40-epoch budget was the binding constraint. The deficit against the unaugmented condition falls from 1.42 points at 40 epochs to 0.38 at 80, against a 0.40-point spread between the augmented seeds: extending the budget alone removed most of the difference, which confirms the earlier reading and is a methodological result in its own right. On balanced accuracy the intervention therefore does nothing. What it does change is the failure mode. Smoothed validation loss, a centred five-epoch rolling mean, used because the augmented curves spike in both directions and the pointwise minimum is unreliable, as the spurious 0.0570 at epoch 75 in this run shows bottoms at epoch 73 against 55 unaugmented, and the train/validation ratio at epoch 80 is 2.57x against 3.97x. Final training loss is 0.079 against 0.025: the augmented model cannot memorise the training set as easily, which is the mechanism by construction.

name: cnn_gap_80_none_geom_photo_s43
notes: Replication of run 014. Smoothed validation loss bottoms at epoch 76 against 53 for the same seed unaugmented, and the train/validation ratio at epoch 80 is 2.43x against 6.57x. Taken with run 014 the onset moves from epochs 53-55 to epochs 73-76 with no overlap between the two conditions, and the severity is roughly halved on both seeds. Caveat: both augmented minima fall at epochs 73 and 76 of an 80-epoch budget, so as at 40 epochs the budget again bounds the measurement - the delay is at least twenty epochs and may be larger. Verdict for the two runs together: augmentation buys no accuracy at a fixed budget and should not be reported as an improvement; it roughly doubles the time before memorisation and halves its severity, so it is what makes a longer budget usable rather than a gain on its own. Kept on that basis.
